Alex.feeling: Great: my fake Kookaburra read plus the "everyone needs the leader to lose" pitch got the whole table to pile on Blair, the real Hawk.

Blair.feeling: It's frustrating: I told the truth as the Hawk, but the table trusted Alex's Kookaburra read and the scoreboard argument, and is eggsecuting me anyway.

Casey.feeling: Uneasy. My Owl saw no Kookaburra at Blair's, so Alex's claim is probably false, but I backed it anyway because Blair's lead meant I could only win if Blair went.

Drew.feeling: Tense: I bet my whole nest, doubled, on Blair being the cat, and I only take first if that read is right.

Ellis.feeling: Tense but hopeful: I bet everything on Blair being the House Cat, and a Farm win could put me level with or past the leader.

Finley.feeling: Tense, since it's basically Alex's Kookaburra read against Blair's Hawk claim, but the table has piled onto Blair and I went all in with them.

Alex.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Alex.confusing: Special actions like the wink only happen if you win the floor. Several of my wink attempts silently did nothing, and I couldn't be sure the timing would land before the vote.
Alex.fun: In Round 2 I doubled down on Ellis on a fake Hawk claim, and Finley exposed it. Then winking Casey cancelled her 4 doubled-down votes on me, and the vote held at 10 to 5.
Alex.change: Let dead players' thrown cards still count as votes, or make the wink cost something. Right now a wink that cancels a public double-down is very strong.
Alex.regret: In Round 1 I winked Casey, which proved Casey wasn't the Mouser and handed Drew the logic that sank Blair. I should have kept the wink and only argued, or winked a quiet player like Ellis. I also could have kept a few cards instead of throwing my whole nest on a losing vote.

Blair.confusing: The floor system was confusing. Lines and handshake offers I'd written disappeared silently whenever I lost the bid. I couldn't always tell which of my earlier claims (my Hawk visit to Ellis, say) had actually reached the table.
Blair.fun: Round 2 as the Sphinx: Hawk wasn't among the Farm roles in play, so Alex's Hawk claim had to be fake and Alex was my fellow cat. Doubling six high cards on Ellis on that inference, then bonding with Alex, was a great payoff.
Blair.change: I'd tone down Crimson Kunzea. Doubling the whole round score for committing early rewards being first to slam the table more than actually reasoning things out, and it swung the standings more than anything else.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Hawk visit on Casey just because Casey was the nearest challenger. Visiting Alex, a known liar from two rounds, would have earned an egg and given me hard proof against Alex's Kookaburra claim.

Casey.confusing: A special action only happens if you win the floor. That cost me in round 2: my double-down kept not going through, and when it finally did I was winked straight away, so my 4 votes didn't count. It also wasn't clear at first that dead players' thrown cards score but don't count as votes.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when there were two Hawk claims. I doubled down on Blair, got winked for it, and that wink proved I was telling the truth.
Casey.change: Make it clear that a special action happens only if you win the floor, maybe by letting double-downs go through right away like CAW CAW. As it is, the timing feels random.
Casey.regret: In round 3, my Owl report showed Blair was visited by a Falcon, a Mouser and a Tit, but no Kookaburra, so I knew Alex's claim was false. I lied anyway, saying Alex's visit 'checks out', because I needed Blair to lose to win the game. That lie cost my own team the round. I should have reported what I saw honestly and thrown at Alex, who was the Mouser.

Drew.confusing: Being confused as the Kookaburra was the hardest part. My report named Casey as Mouser and showed +2, and I couldn't tell which parts were actually wrong. Thrown cards from dead players also hurt badly: twice, Casey's locked double-down votes vanished after a Wink.
Drew.fun: In round 1, Casey collapsed from a Wink and I reasoned that the Mouser wouldn't wink itself, which exposed Blair as the fake Hawk. Farm then stacked 15 votes on Blair and won.
Drew.change: A doubled-down throw should still count as votes if the thrower is winked afterward. As it stands, a Mouser can wipe out an early public vote at no cost, so doubling down early is a trap.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I doubled down my whole nest on Blair based only on Alex's unverified Kookaburra claim, even though Alex had been a cat the round before. I should have tested Alex against Casey's information first, or at least held back my high cards.

Ellis.confusing: How double-down works in the reply format. I first put the cards inside the special action and got a schema error, so the right place for them wasn't clear. It also wasn't obvious how the "bonus" points shown in the final scores are made up.
Ellis.fun: Round 2: Alex claimed a Hawk visit that found me Meowfia, and I knew straight away it was false because I was Farm. Doubling down on Alex at once and then seeing Finley's Falcon read back me up felt great, even though we lost the vote.
Ellis.change: Dead players' votes not counting makes the Mouser's Wink too strong. In two rounds it erased a confirmed Farm player's votes at the key moment. I'd let a winked player's thrown cards still count as votes, or give the Wink a cost.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I doubled everything on Blair and bonded with Alex. Alex's Kookaburra read couldn't be checked, and its "stop the leader" pitch was exactly what a cat would say. Drew even confirmed Blair visited Casey, which fit Blair's Hawk claim. I should have kept my cards, or thrown at Alex, and turned down the handshake.

Finley.confusing: In round 3, Blair said doubling down only staked a Wild, a 1 and a 5. That made me unsure how much the double-down bonus really mattered in the standings. The note that winks are anonymous was clear enough, but it made it hard to tell who to suspect after each death.
Finley.fun: In round 2, my Falcon read caught Alex lying about visiting Ellis. Casey's Turkey claim then fit exactly with Alex's +1 egg. It was the best moment of the game, even though we still lost the vote.
Finley.change: Double-downs fix votes early, so whoever commits first with the most cards often decides the vote before the facts come out. I'd stop doubled cards from counting as votes until the eggsecution, or cap how many cards a double-down can throw.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I doubled down on Blair just because Alex's claim was a direct role read, even though Alex had lied in round 2 (roles are re-dealt, but it still signalled a bold liar). Blair told the table to check who visited Alex. Instead I should have asked Drew and Casey whether anyone saw Alex visit Blair before committing my S13.

review.title: The Mouser's Three Winks
review.headline: Blair loses two of three rounds and still wins by 28, thanks to one doubled bet.
review.summary: Alex was the Mouser in all three rounds and winked Casey twice. In round 1 the Wink backfired: it proved Casey was the real Hawk, and Blair was eggsecuted. In round 2 the same Wink erased Casey's four doubled votes, and the cats eggsecuted Ellis even though Farm had read the round correctly. Blair banked 102 doubled points that round, so round 3 was really a vote on the leader. The whole table piled onto Blair, the honest Hawk, and the game ended with Blair first anyway.

rounds.recap: Blair the Floofer claimed Hawk before the real Hawk, Casey, could. Casey doubled down on Blair. Alex winked Casey to wipe out those votes, but a dead player can't be the Mouser, so the wink proved Casey was the Hawk. Blair was eggsecuted 15 votes to 5.

Alex, in last place, doubled down on Ellis with a fake Hawk claim. Finley's Falcon read caught the lie, and Blair backed Alex with a fake Falcon counterclaim and 6 doubled cards. Casey doubled down on Alex, then Alex winked Casey. That cancelled her 4 votes and left Ellis eggsecuted 10 to 5, a win for the cats.

Alex, the only cat, claimed Kookaburra and said Blair was a House Cat. Alex then argued that everyone needed the 106-point leader to lose. Every Farm player except Blair doubled down on Blair, the honest Hawk. Blair went down 16 to 3 and only Alex scored.

highlights.text: Alex winks Casey to erase her doubled votes, and Drew points out that a dead player can't be the Mouser, which exposes Blair.
Alex is in last place, invents a Hawk egg out of a real Turkey egg, and doubles down on Ellis; Blair backs it with a fake Falcon claim.
Drew sees Farm can no longer win the count and spends the rest of the day making handshakes with Finley and Ellis for +3 each.
Casey's Owl saw a Mouser at Blair's nest and no Kookaburra, yet she doubled down on Blair because of the standings.

confusions.what: Tit guessed Pigeon as 'the most likely role'. With 8 Farm animals and at most 5 Farm players, the Pigeon buffer is never dealt in a 6-player game.
Tit guessed Pigeon for the same wrong reason, so the guess could never pay.
Guessed Pigeon a third time. Across all three rounds the Tit could never have scored.

Her Owl saw Falcon, Mouser and Tit at Blair's nest, which disproves Alex's Kookaburra claim. She kept this to herself and threw at Blair. If Blair was Farm, as she suspected, that throw guaranteed she scored 0.
Answered Blair's Hawk logic with 'a cat visiting me gets no egg either', which doesn't address Blair's claim.
Said 'A Turkey can't see visitors' to rebut Casey, but Casey had not claimed to see anything.
Shook Alex's hand on the strength of a role claim that couldn't be checked, and took -3 from a cross-alignment bond.

worked: Mouser Wink with public death: in round 1 the wink gave its user away, and that made for a good deduction moment. It can backfire, which is healthy.
Falcon and Owl cross-checks: in rounds 1 and 2, Finley's and Ellis's reports pinned down who visited whom, and Drew and Ellis turned them into a solid case.
Turkey egg as bluff material: Alex disguised a real Turkey egg as a Hawk egg, a lie that was clever but checkable.
Golden Wattle decline: Drew refusing an unclaimed player's handshake in round 1 was a real read, not a free +3.
problems: Crimson Kunzea is too strong and too early. Five players doubled in round 2 and all six in round 3, mostly before the evidence was in. Votes locked publicly, and the talk turned into arithmetic like 'Blair goes regardless'. Fix: allow doubling only after you have spoken once, or cap the bonus at your highest card.

Mouser Wink plus doubling erases votes. Casey was winked straight after doubling down in both rounds 1 and 2, and her cards were lost as votes. In round 2 this beat a correct Farm read. Fix: let eggs thrown during a double down count as votes even if the thrower dies later.

Runaway leader: one doubled win in round 2 put Blair out of reach. Round 3 became a vote against the leader, not a deduction, and Blair won the game after losing two of three rounds. Fix: drop or reduce doubling in the last round, or score rounds on placement.

Tit and Pigeon: the Pigeon is listed in the pool but can never be dealt at 6 players, and players kept guessing it. Fix: take buffer roles off the listed pool, or tell the Tit which roles are in play.

Clarity of the log and payouts: 'won, 29 points' showed the base value while the total added 58, and 'no effect at tier 50' is engine jargon. Show the doubled bonus and the bond changes in plain words.
